services.name: Past Exhibits
services.desc: 2027 marks the 10-year anniversary of the Wild Gardens’ opening to the public. With this exhibition, we will kick off a year-long celebration of plants indigenous to the Ukiah Valley and the broader region that spans southern Mendocino County, Lake County, and northern Sonoma County. The exhibition will explore the importance of native plants to the region’s ecosystems, the relationships that Pomo peoples have maintained with them though their care and use over thousands of years, and our communal responsibility to protect them. services.desc: Docent led tours of the historic Sun House are generally available Friday through Sunday from 12:00 to 3:00.Please call to confirm tour availability, or to inquire aboutscheduling a tour for the day you plan to visit. The Sun House, a 1911 redwood Craftsman bungalow home, is situated immediately in front of the Museum and is available for tours. Grace and John Hudson, its owners, together with architect George Wilcox, set out to build a functional, custom Craftsman-style home scaled to the Hudsons’ needs.
